page: Vultr vhp-1c-2gb-intel is a shared-core virtual machine belonging to the High Performance server family. It features a single Intel Xeon x86_64 vCPU operating at 2.0 GHz, paired with 2.0 GB of system memory. Storage is provided via a local 50 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No dedicated GPU is present on this configuration.

Benchmark data indicates that the single-core stress-ng performance is in the average range at 1421.58, but multi-core performance is limited by the single-thread configuration, placing it in the bottom 10%. Memory bandwidth is relatively low, with read-only large block speeds at 7.43 GB/sec and write speeds at 6.32 GB/sec. Single-threaded gzip compression performs at 23.24 GB/sec, while PassMark CPU and memory scores fall into the bottom 10% of tested hardware.

Given its shared CPU allocation and entry-level hardware specifications, this server type represents a highly cost-efficient option for lightweight workloads that do not require dedicated compute resources. The primary tradeoff is the shared CPU model and low memory capacity, which limits its ability to handle concurrent multi-threaded tasks or memory-intensive applications.

This instance is best suited for basic general-purpose workloads, such as lightweight static web serving, simple scripting, development environments, or small-scale Redis caching operations where high-throughput multi-core processing is not required.
